explanation: Test odd starting values in increasing order using BigInt arithmetic. Track the current trajectory to detect cycles, and stop after reaching a value smaller than the start because its convergence has already been established.
timeComplexity: O(T), where T is the number of trajectory steps examined T counts actual examined trajectory steps; no unsupported logarithmic or polynomial convergence bound is assumed.
spaceComplexity: O(S), where S is the longest examined trajectory segment Storage depends on distinct trajectory/cache values rather than just n; big integers also depend on bit length.
attribution: JavaScript port of the independently authored EPI Practice C# algorithm; no upstream reference code copied.
correctness: Each examined start stops only after reaching a smaller positive value, whose convergence has already been established directly or through its smaller odd part. A repeated value in the current segment detects a cycle. Induction over starts proves the claimed range when no cycle or arithmetic overflow occurs.
walkthrough: For n=5, the nontrivial starts are 3 and 5. Their paths enter smaller values: 3→10→5→16→8→4→2 and 5→16→8→4. Those smaller values converge to 1, so return true.
edgeCases: For n≤2 no nontrivial trajectory is needed.
Even starts immediately reduce to smaller values.
BigInt avoids fixed-width wraparound; no general polynomial bound on trajectory length is known.
